title: amenbo: a Japanese-web-native MCP server for low-impact, token-efficient web collection
description:
amenbo (アメンボ / water strider) is an MCP server for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Like the insect gliding across water without making ripples, it collects information from the web with minimal load on target sites and minimal token consumption, optimized especially for Japanese websites. It also runs as a CLI sharing the same core.

Token efficiency: outline-to-section progressive disclosure (fetch only the sections you need), diff-only responses on refetch, CJK-aware content pruning using punctuation density and character-class ratios, automatic Markdown/screenshot switching, and CJK-weighted token estimation.

Japanese-web handling: main-content inference from rendered geometry for loosely structured pages, automatic Shift_JIS / EUC-JP / ISO-2022-JP detection, ruby (furigana) stripping, screenshot fallback for image-rendered information, restoration of high-link-density tables and headings dropped by generic content extraction, and dedicated adapters for Qiita, Zenn, note, Hatena Blog, Yahoo! News and PR TIMES.

Low impact: two-tier fetching (plain HTTP first, headless Chromium only when JS rendering is required), robots.txt and Crawl-Delay compliance, per-domain serialized access at 1 req/sec by default, sitemap/RSS-preferred link discovery, ETag / If-Modified-Since revalidation, and an honest self-identifying User-Agent. No anti-bot circumvention is implemented.

Source code: github.com/Rererr/amenbo · npm: amenbo. The benchmark harness and raw logs used to compare amenbo against comparable tools are included under bench/.
